geography.description: Pasay lies on the western coast of Metro Manila, facing Manila Bay. Its coastal neighborhoods, inland communities and airport area connect the city to the rest of the capital.

history.title: Namayan and a local origin story
history.description: The city traces its early settlement to Namayan. Its account presents Dayang-dayang Pasay, the princess associated with the city’s name, as a local story.

history.title: The name Pineda
history.description: The city’s history records the name Pineda during the Spanish colonial period.

history.title: A town of its own
history.description: Pineda became an independent town. Pasay commemorates this date as its foundation day.

history.title: Pasay and Malibay
history.description: The name Pasay returned in 1901. The neighboring town of Malibay was incorporated in 1903.

history.title: War and rebuilding
history.description: Pasay emerged from the destruction of the Second World War and began rebuilding its communities.

history.title: Cityhood as Rizal City
history.description: Republic Act No. 183 established the city, initially named Rizal City.

history.title: Pasay City again
history.description: The city’s name officially returned to Pasay City.

history.title: PICC opens
history.description: The Philippine International Convention Center opened, adding a major convention and cultural venue to the city.

history.title: Barangay 201 in law
history.description: Republic Act No. 11403 provided for Barangay 201, Zone 20, separating Kalayaan Village, Teachers Bliss and Balabag from Barangay 183, subject to the law’s plebiscite provisions.

places.name: Cultural Center of the Philippines
places.description: A home for theater, music, dance and visual arts in the CCP Complex. Explore its current program when planning a visit.

places.name: Philippine International Convention Center
places.description: Designed by National Artist Leandro V. Locsin, the PICC opened in 1976. Its complex and intrinsic artworks are recognized as National Cultural Treasures.

places.name: Cuneta Astrodome
places.description: A city-operated indoor arena used for sporting competitions, civic gatherings and community events since 1993.

places.name: SM Mall of Asia
places.description: A waterfront shopping, dining and entertainment destination on reclaimed land along Manila Bay.

places.name: Sta. Clara de Montefalco Parish
places.description: A Spanish-era parish highlighted in the city’s tourism directory for its church architecture and local history.

places.name: Seaside Dampa Macapagal
places.description: A seafood market and dining destination known for choosing fresh seafood and having it cooked at nearby restaurants.

leadership.role: Represents Pasay in the House of Representatives.

barangayNotes.grouping: The PSA lists all 201 numbered barangays under Pasay City. The city profile identifies 20 zones and two local districts; individual zone and district assignments are not provided in the PSA table and have not been transcribed here.
